static_findings.snippet: *Open-source Splice 0.5.4 ships with SDK snapshot `3.3.0-snapshot.20250502` (pre-dates LF 2.2). LF 2
Package IDs are cryptographic hashes of: source content + LF version (`--target`) + SDK/stdlib versi
4. Remove `-Wno-ledger-time-is-alpha` from all `daml.yaml` files (not in SDK 3.4.9)
5. Build: `daml build -p daml/splice-util && daml build -p daml/splice-amulet`
**"Unknown Daml-LF version: 2.2"**: damlc binary doesn't support 2.2. Check `daml damlc --help` for
**Package ID mismatch**: different `--target` values between builds. Check: `unzip -p package.dar ME

content.value_statement: Canton, DAML, and Splice version choices can create package mismatches and build failures. This skill gives repo maps, LF version guidance, and troubleshooting checks.
actual_capabilities: Maps Splice, Canton, and DAML SDK version relationships for Canton Network work.
Identifies repository files that control LF versions, package targets, Docker builds, and Canton versions.
Explains how LF targets, SDK versions, and dependencies affect DAML package IDs.
Provides build command references for community Canton participants and Splice applications.
Guides troubleshooting for unsupported LF versions, package ID mismatches, and upgrade validation failures.
limitations: It is a static reference and does not verify current repository releases.
It focuses on Canton Network, DAML, and Splice repositories only.
It does not replace testing, ledger validation, or upstream release notes.
Version examples may become outdated as repositories change.

use_cases.title: Review Version Alignment
use_cases.description: Compare Splice, Canton, and DAML SDK versions before changing LF targets or package dependencies.

use_cases.title: Debug Package Mismatches
use_cases.description: Trace package ID differences caused by LF targets, SDK versions, source changes, or dependency changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Repository Builds
use_cases.description: Find key build files and commands for community Canton participants and Splice applications.

prompt_templates.title: Map Repository Versions
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation for Canton Network repositories.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how Splice, Canton, and DAML SDK versions relate. Include LF defaults and available LF versions.

prompt_templates.title: Locate Build Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Find files that control LF and SDK behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list the repository files I should inspect before changing DAML LF targets in Splice and Canton.

prompt_templates.title: Plan LF Upgrade
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a controlled LF target update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the steps for upgrading Splice packages to LF 2.2 with SDK 3.4.9.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Package ID Drift
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting for incompatible DAR packages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose why community-built DARs have different package IDs from enterprise DARs. Focus on LF target, SDK version, and dependencies.

output_examples.input: I need to understand how Splice, Canton, and DAML versions relate.
output_examples.output: A compatibility summary that explains repository roles, LF availability, and the recommended SDK upgrade path.

output_examples.input: My package IDs changed after rebuilding DAR files.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering LF target values, SDK versions, dependency package IDs, and source differences.

output_examples.input: I want to build a community Canton participant.
output_examples.output: A concise build preparation guide with the target repository, expected artifact, and prerequisites to confirm first.

best_practices: Confirm SDK, LF target, and dependency package IDs before rebuilding DARs.
Check upstream release notes before applying the documented version examples.
Run build and inspection commands only inside trusted repository checkouts.
anti_patterns: Mixing LF targets across related packages without a migration plan.
Assuming community and enterprise artifacts match without verifying SDK and LF versions.
Running build commands in unknown repositories or with unreviewed scripts.

faq.question: What repositories does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Splice, Canton, and the DAML SDK in Canton Network development workflows.

faq.question: Can it verify the latest upstream release?
faq.answer: No. It is a static reference, so check upstream release pages for current versions.

faq.question: Why do LF targets matter?
faq.answer: LF targets affect package IDs and compatibility. Different targets can make otherwise similar packages incompatible.

faq.question: Does it run build commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It only documents commands and files that a developer may review or run.

faq.question: Can it help with package ID mismatches?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists likely causes, including LF target changes, SDK changes, dependency changes, and source changes.

faq.question: Is it only for enterprise Canton users?
faq.answer: No. It compares community and enterprise context and includes community Canton build guidance.
